classification.difficultyReason: Use converse angle tests to distinguish parallel and nonparallel line pairs and justify the conclusions.

content.prompt:
For each diagram, state whether the diagram has parallel lines.
Justify your answer using angle relationships.

spec.description: Two near-vertical lines lean right upwards; a gently rising transversal crosses both. Six continuation arrowheads. The two marked sectors are below the transversal and between the steep lines.
spec.mathematics: Co-interior angles 113° and 67°. No parallel markings are given.
spec.answerVisibility: Both angle measurements are permanent givens. The supplied blue conclusion belongs only in the answer.

answer.worked:
$113^\circ+67^\circ=180^\circ$.
The co-interior angles sum to $180^\circ$, so the lines are parallel.

spec.description: Two steep lines descend rightwards, with the right line more inclined. A descending transversal crosses both. Six continuation arrowheads; both marked interior sectors are above the transversal.
spec.mathematics: Co-interior angles 124° and 46°. Their sum is 170°. No parallel markings are given.
spec.answerVisibility: Measurements are question givens; the supplied conclusion is answer-only.

answer.short: No. Co-interior angles do not sum to $180^\circ$.
answer.worked:
$124^\circ+46^\circ=170^\circ$.
The co-interior angles do not sum to $180^\circ$, so the lines are not parallel.

spec.description: Two steep rising lines meet a descending transversal. Both 77° sectors occupy the bottom position at their intersections. All six line endpoints have continuation arrowheads.

answer.worked: The corresponding angles are both $77^\circ$, so the lines are parallel.

spec.description: Two steep rising lines are crossed by a descending transversal. The 79° and 74° sectors lie between the up-right steep rays and up-left transversal rays. Six continuation arrowheads.
